target_customer: US community banks, credit unions and fintech-bank programs that pay for digital account opening and onboarding software
problem: Banks lose applicants because consumer and business account opening is slow and manual, and core systems make it hard to digitize.
business_model: B2B SaaS white-label platform sold to banks, with core and digital banking integrations (Finastra, Q2, Abrigo)
product_category: Banking as a service, digital account opening and onboarding

founders.name: Chris Blaser
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built electric race cars at CalSol; a press summary calls him CTO. No education listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard workflow software, but it needed integrations with legacy bank core systems and compliance steps such as identity and business ownership checks, which are slow to build for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Once a bank embeds onboarding in its core and digital banking stack, switching is costly. Bank sales cycles are long, which also slows rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Core vendors such as Finastra became integration partners rather than copying it, per 2024 press. No acquisition of Prelim was found.

market_need_then: Banks were under pressure from fintechs and online banks to offer fast digital onboarding, and the YC page and later press show demand from community banks. No dated 2017 evidence was opened, so this is an inference from later coverage.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise fintech press release voice in partner announcements

brand_strength.rationale: Only B2B partnership press found; no brand-focused coverage, merch or community. The company name appears to have been Original Tech at YC, per CB Insights listings, with no reason found.

outcome_analysis: Prelim is still operating independently as a bank onboarding platform with partnerships with Finastra, Abrigo, Q2, Lead Bank and Vantage Bank through 2025. Public funding data is thin, so growth is judged from bank customer wins and a best-in-class ranking in the ABA 2024 assessment rather than from capital raised.
notes: Funding only seen on aggregators: Employbl (Diffbot data) lists about $4M total, a $2M seed with Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, Fuel Capital, S2 Capital, Ryan Petersen and Max Altman, and a separate $2M round with EJF Capital; VCBacked lists the same investors. Treated as unverified, so no rounds are recorded. No dated 2017 competitor source was found; later directories list Mantl, Tyfone, Narmi, Amount, Lumin Digital, which are not dated to the batch. Company site fetch returned only a title.
